programName: Bachelor of Science in Computer Science and Engineering
department: Department of Computer Science and Engineering
background: The BS CSE program is offered through Ohio State's College of Engineering.
The program combines engineering, physical sciences, mathematics, and intensive computer science coursework.
Ohio State's Department of Computer Science and Engineering was founded in 1968.
The department offers undergraduate and graduate programs including BS CSE, BS CIS, BA CIS, MS CSE, and PhD CSE.

CSE research areas include artificial intelligence, computer graphics, data management, high performance computing, networking and distributed systems, security, software engineering, systems, programming languages, and theory.

requirements.name: CSE Core
requirements.description: All BS CSE students must complete the required core CSE sequence. The local course database stores CSE 2501 / PHILOS ethics content as part of the core requirement.
notes: Official OSU page lists the CSE core courses and their prerequisites.
Core courses include CSE 2221, CSE 2231, CSE 2321, CSE 2331, CSE 2421, CSE 2431, CSE 3341, and an ethics/professional issues course.
Students entering AU22 or later may use CSE 2501 or PHILOS 2338 for the ethics requirement; students who entered before AU22 or have permission to use Legacy GE may take PHILOS 1338.
Several core courses require earlier CSE, math, statistics, or writing coursework; always check the individual course prerequisite text.

requirements.name: CSE Core Choices
requirements.description: Students choose five additional CSE courses from required decision areas: software engineering or databases, architecture or networking, AI or game/animation, project, and capstone.
notes: The decision areas are: software engineering or databases; computer architecture or networking; AI or game/animation; project; capstone.
Software engineering or databases: CSE 3231 or CSE 3241.
Computer architecture or networking: CSE 3421 or CSE 3461.
AI or game/animation: CSE 3521 or CSE 3541.
Project: one of CSE 3901, CSE 3902, or CSE 3903.
Capstone: one of the CSE 591X capstone options shown in the official program information.
Some core choices may also satisfy specialization requirements, depending on the student's specialization.

requirements.name: Technical Electives
requirements.description: All BS CSE students must complete 17 credit hours of technical elective coursework.
notes: At least 9 technical elective credits must be in CSE.
The remaining 8 credits may be additional CSE 3000-level or higher courses not already counting toward another degree requirement, or approved non-CSE courses.
Some technical electives are determined by the student's selected specialization option.
Do not count a course twice: a course already used for core, core choice, capstone, math/science, GE, or another requirement should not also be counted as a technical elective.
CSE courses graded S/U or focused on research have special credit limits.
No more than 2 credit hours from CSE 4251, CSE 4252, CSE 4253, and CSE 4256 may count toward technical electives.
No more than 6 credit hours total from CSE 4193, CSE 4998, and CSE 4999 may count toward technical electives.
Non-CSE technical electives must be part of a completed minor, appear on the pre-approved outside technical elective list, or be approved by petition.

requirements.name: Math and Science Electives
requirements.description: BS CSE students must complete 8 credits of approved math and/or science electives.
notes: The local database includes the approved options shown on the OSU BS CSE program information page and GOLD curriculum materials.
These are choices, not all required courses. Students choose enough approved options to reach 8 credits.

requirements.name: General Education
requirements.description: Engineering students need 24 credits in General Education.
notes: The app treats GE entries as placeholders because GE course choices depend on the engineering GE rules and student selections.
Use OSU Engineering GE materials or advising resources for detailed GE category breakdowns.

requirements.name: Non-Computer Science Core
requirements.description: BS CSE students complete supplemental non-CSE core courses in engineering, digital logic, mathematics, and statistics.
notes: Official current BS CSE information lists ECE 2360, ECE 2060, MATH 2568, MATH 3345, and STAT 3470.
ECE 2360 is required for students who entered the program in or after AU22. Students who entered prior to AU22 may take ECE 2020, but ECE 2360 is preferred.
Older GOLD curriculum materials may show ECE 2020 instead of ECE 2360.

technicalElectiveRules: At least 9 of the 17 credits must be CSE coursework.
CSE technical elective candidates are generally CSE courses at the 3000 level or higher that are not already counting toward another degree requirement.
The remaining technical elective credits may be additional eligible CSE courses or approved non-CSE courses at the 2000 level or higher.
Non-CSE technical electives must be from a completed minor, from the pre-approved outside technical elective list, or approved by petition.
No more than 2 credits from CSE 4251, CSE 4252, CSE 4253, and CSE 4256 may count toward technical electives.
No more than 6 credits total from CSE 4193, CSE 4998, and CSE 4999 may count toward technical electives.
Specialization requirements may determine part of the student's technical elective choices.

specializationOptions.name: Artificial Intelligence
specializationOptions.summary: Focuses on AI techniques and related advanced AI electives.
requirements: Additional AI specialization courses should be checked against the official specialization page because options can change.

specializationOptions.name: Computer Graphics and Game Design
specializationOptions.summary: Focuses on game development, graphics, animation, and interactive systems.
requirements: Additional graphics/game specialization courses should be checked against the official specialization page because options can change.

specializationOptions.name: Database Systems and Data Analytics
specializationOptions.summary: Focuses on database systems, data management, and analytics.
requirements: Additional database/data analytics specialization courses should be checked against the official specialization page because options can change.

specializationOptions.name: Information and Computation Assurance
requirements: CSE 3461 and security-focused electives are commonly relevant; check the official specialization page for the exact current list.

specializationOptions.name: Computer Networking
specializationOptions.summary: Focuses on networks, distributed systems, and related security/network electives.
requirements: CSE 3461 and networking-focused electives are commonly relevant; check the official specialization page for the exact current list.

specializationOptions.name: Computer Systems
specializationOptions.summary: Focuses on computer architecture, operating systems, parallel computing, and systems-level topics.
requirements: CSE 3421 and systems-focused electives are commonly relevant; check the official specialization page for the exact current list.

specializationOptions.name: Software Engineering
specializationOptions.summary: Focuses on software requirements, design, implementation, and applied software systems.
requirements: One additional approved software engineering specialization course from the official specialization page.

specializationOptions.name: Individualized Option
specializationOptions.summary: Allows a student to build a focused plan with advising support.
requirements: Students should consult academic advisors to identify an appropriate course set for their interests.

advisingNotes: Do not calculate graduation completion by summing every course option in the database. Many rows are choices, not required courses.
When answering student questions, distinguish between required credits and available course-option credits.
This app is a planning assistant, not an official degree audit.
For official degree audits, students should confirm requirements with OSU advising and the current OSU curriculum materials.

If a student asks whether a specific course will count for a requirement, answer from the available local data but recommend confirming with advising when the rule depends on specialization, petition approval, catalog year, GE status, or transfer credit.
